description: OriDB v3.0 trial release: the Confirmed origin tier only, carried forward from OriDB v2 with explicit evidence records.
inclusion_rule: An origin is Confirmed if its interval overlaps at least one plasmid (ARS) assay positive or one 2D gel electrophoresis record.

sacCer3.note: Lifted from sacCer1 with the UCSC chain file. Each record keeps its original sacCer1 position in source_chromosome/source_start/source_end and the outcome of a base-for-base sequence check in lift_status.

provenance.source: nieduszy_oridb MySQL dump (OriDB v2.1.0 cerevisiae / v1.0.0 pombe)

known_issues.text: Non-Confirmed v2 origins that overlap direct evidence and need curator review: sc_ori 79 (Dubious), sc_ori 84 (Dubious), sc_ori 741 (Likely). They are Likely or Dubious in v2, so they are not in this release and cannot be linked here.

Positions will not coincide with the ARS features UCSC and SGD show for sacCer3. OriDB intervals are the experimentally assayed regions reported by the source studies - for the plasmid data, the PCR fragment that conferred ARS activity - which are larger objects than an annotated ARS element. This is expected, not an error. A coordinate-convention offset has been excluded for the largest contributing study (Nieduszynski 2006, PMID 16847347): its PCR primers were located in sacCer1 by sequence and the 5' and 3' ends of 199 of its 228 fragments sit exactly on the recorded coordinates, confirming them as 1-based inclusive. No fragment was contradicted. Of the other 29, 21 yielded no primer at either end (19 of those being ARSs taken from earlier literature rather than amplified in that study, so no primers exist for them); the remaining 8 have oligos nearby but none landing exactly, each 5 bp or more away and so a different oligo rather than the amplification primer. No fragment end has a primer 1-4 bp off as its only candidate. The remaining plasmid and 2D gel sources have not been checked this way at all.

51 lifted cerevisiae intervals do not have identical sequence in sacCer3 - substitutions, or an indel that changes interval length. Each mapping was checked and is correctly placed; it is the 2003 assembly sequence that was revised. Intervals whose length changed are worth a curator review. The origins affected are:

lift.note: Systematic names are NOT recomputed. They are coordinate-derived labels from the v2 build and are cited as such in the literature, so they stay fixed; a name like X-212 therefore need not match the lifted midpoint.
